issues: High — bounded_process can leave an unregistered running child after an ordinary identity-read failure. Immediately after Popen succeeds, it calls process_identity before on_spawn. If that lookup raises, finally calls terminate_group, whose _terminate_group immediately repeats the same lookup. A persistent OSError or PermissionError reading the child's /proc entry or boot identity therefore prevents both registration and termination. If the lookup instead repeatedly returns None, cleanup can also fail to find members and reach proc.wait(timeout=5) while the child remains alive. The parent then unwinds without a durable identity available to recover_process. This is an accidental failure after a successful fork, not the excluded uncatchable-kill window. Repair by establishing an exception-safe cleanup path for a newly created, unreaped direct child that does not depend on the metadata read that failed. Under the stated no-other-reaper assumption, retain the child as the ownership anchor, terminate its known initial group with bounded escalation, and reap only after cleanup. Persist unresolved cleanup state if termination cannot be established; never silently resume from an absent active-process record.
